youtube.title: A Tan Is a Tiny Parasol Over Each Cell
youtube.caption:
What is a tan, really? Pigment, parked over each cell's nucleus.

The more melanin a cell held, the more protection it had. So the shield is real, but its strength varies from cell to cell. In lab-grown skin cells, the long rays, UVA, set off cap-building through a light sensor. So a tan is pigment gathered over each cell's nucleus. It lowers damage, but does not erase it.

Series: Season 2: What your skin does, part 4 of 6. Next: the brick wall on your skin

Sources
1. UV-induced redistribution of melanin near keratinocyte nuclei leads to the formation of a supranuclear cap. — NIH: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/36869204/
2. The epidermal-melanin unit is one melanocyte and about 36 neighbouring keratinocytes; melanin is synthesized in melanosomes. — NIH: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/11549105/
3. In irradiated human skin explants, epidermal cells with supranuclear melanin caps had significantly less DNA photoproducts than cells without caps. — NIH: https://pubmed.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/9579550/

Narration: synthetic voice (AI). Illustrations: AI-generated and 3-D animation made in code, no stock footage. Every number's source is listed in this description.

Education, not medical advice. See a dermatologist about your own skin.
